title: Directional token attribution pilot with streaming-minimum opt-out for enterprise pilots
creator: Elena Rodriguez
description:
Goal: Run a controlled pilot to evaluate a per-direction token attribution model (separate ingress/input and egress/output rates) alongside an optional streaming-minimum opt-out for enterprise customers with strict SSO/KMS/compliance needs. We want to measure billing accuracy, revenue neutrality across cohorts, developer friction, and legal/contract lift required for offering opt-outs on minimums to enterprise customers.

Scope:
- Hosted API only (no Dedicated/Private for this pilot)
- Focus on conversational/chat workloads with long streaming responses and high token ratio variance
- Metric collection: per-request ingress/egress token counts, streaming vs non-streaming flags, latency, percent of requests hitting cached prefixes

Non-goals: changing free tier or usage quotas, not touching reserved capacity/Dedicated pricebooks in this pilot.
acceptance_criteria: Instrument billing pipeline to emit per-request ingress and egress token counts to experiments BigQuery table
Run 4-week AB test with 3 enterprise pilot accounts vs matched control using current symmetric per-token pricing
Demonstrate no >7% negative revenue delta for Redwood across pilot cohort after normalizing for usage pattern shifts
Document contract language required to allow explicit streaming-minimum opt-out and legal sign-off from Revenue Ops
Provide rollout decision memo with recommended default pricing (symmetric vs directional) and enterprise opt-out policy
metrics: Revenue delta (pilot vs control) - normalized to baseline month
Average ingress:egress token ratio per session
% of streaming sessions electing opt-out when offered
Client-side integration friction (number of support tickets tagged 'billing-change')
rollout_plan: Week 0: Instrumentation and validation - ENG implements per-request token tagging and test ingest to staging
Week 1: Internal dry run with synthetic workloads and lifecycle tests (billing reconciliation + dashboard)
Week 2-5: Run pilot with 3 enterprise customers (marketing/legal coordinated) with explicit opt-in to experiment
Week 6: Analyze results, legal sign-off on contract language, prepare PRD for broader rollout if metric targets met
notes: Design trade-off: directional pricing simplifies cost attribution for asymmetric workloads (e.g., search+summarize) but increases complexity in UI and billing exports
Edge case to handle: multi-call streaming where a single logical response is split into multiple streaming frames - ensure attribution ties to request id
We must ensure telemetry includes model variant and quantization profile so we can decompose unit economics by model type
Consider a grace mechanism: allow enterprise customers one billing-cycle opt-out trial before permanent contract amendment

Enterprise legal pushback requiring deeper discounts or longer minimums
Edge-case behaviors for multipart streaming responses could miscount tokens
